requirement:
Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
rationale:
Every obligation of `requirements.definitions.inputs` is carried out by reachable code and has a test that asserts its outcome. I read the code and tests supplied in the inputs. I did not run the tests.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Definition form with exactly `definition` and `text`.**
  - `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_input]` takes the definition branch when the `definition` key is present. It calls `check_keys` with only `definition` and `text`, `string_field` for the name, and `text_field` for the text.
  - `text_field` requires a nonempty array of strings and checks every element.
  - Recording is done by `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[to_input]`, which writes `{definition, text}`.
- **`definition` identifies one named definition.** `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]` looks the name up in the definitions map, keeps only definitions of kind `Term`, and otherwise returns "no matching named definition".
- **`text` holds the complete raw declaration as source lines.** `resolve` returns `redact_lines(&target.raw_lines)`, and `to_input` records that as `text`.
- **Reject missing definitions.** `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_resolved_input]` pushes the resolve error, which names the definition.
- **Reject changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff.** The same function compares the recorded text with the resolved text. On a difference it pushes "input text changed for {selector:?}" followed by `compact_diff`.
- **Moving an unchanged definition does not invalidate its snapshot.** The comparison uses only the raw text, never line numbers or position, so moving a definition cannot change it. Line numbers are recorded only in the resolved ranges, which are not compared.
- **Evidence displays show the definition name, current location and recorded text.**
  - `src/index.rs#fn[render_input]` and `src/index.rs#impl[InputLocation]/fn[resolve]` produce the heading `definition {name}`.
  - They list each range with its name and current file and line range, then print the recorded `text` as a code block.
  - They fall back to the recorded text when the selector no longer resolves.

**Tests**
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[changed_definition_snapshots_show_a_compact_diff_and_text_is_required]` covers:
  - a changed body line, asserting the exact `- …` / `+ …` diff and that the error names `glossary.a`;
  - missing, empty and non-array `text`, each asserted to give an error on `evidence/rules.ready.json` that mentions `text`.
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked]` covers an unexpected extra field and a deleted definition file. The deleted-file case asserts "no matching named definition" with the definition name.
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[cyclic_dependencies_are_required_once_and_changes_require_review]` covers:
  - prepending blank lines to the glossary, which moves every definition, and asserting validation still passes;
  - changes to the phrase option and to the body, each asserted to fail with "input text changed".
- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[detail_page_shows_recorded_text_locations_and_first_matching_group]` covers the display. It asserts the definition name, its file and line-range location and the recorded text appear in that order. It also covers an unresolved definition keeping its recorded text.

I found no unspecified behavior and no unacknowledged gaps.
